title: Power Pages: performance and usage metrics in the Power Platform admin center monitor hub
notes: claim 45: severity major on a rationale: risk; rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
2026-11-16: taken offline; the grace for pages published before the check existed is off
summary: Hold: the briefing tells administrators to treat the capability as included even though its licensing is not published. The roadmap metrics and both documented navigation paths check out, but several assurances about existing monitoring and the new feature's effects go beyond the evidence.

claims.claim: The intended audience for the insights is site owners, makers and administrators.

claims.claim: The monitor hub is the Monitor area of the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Your organization can use the Monitor area of the Power Platform admin center to measure and improve operational health metrics of resources that are built or deployed.

claims.claim: Monitor calculates health metrics by aggregating runtime logs.
claims.quote: Metrics are calculated by aggregating daily event logs from runtime activity; they're not real-time.

claims.claim: The general Monitor experience serves administrators and makers.
claims.quote: The Monitor experience is available to both makers (in experiences such as Power Apps) and admins (in experiences such as the Power Platform admin center).

claims.claim: Access to the general Monitor admin experience is governed by administrative roles.
claims.quote: Admin experiences are available to Power Platform service and Dynamics 365 admins, who can view Monitor data across the tenant.

claims.claim: Power Pages capacity management provides capacity consumption and licensing views.
claims.quote: The Power Pages capacity management experience in the Power Platform admin center allows administrators to manage Power Pages capacity and monitor capacity consumption. This experience also provides an overview of the different licensing models in use.

claims.claim: The action rating none is consistent with the briefing's recommendation that administrators decide how to use and govern the new reporting capability.
claims.quote: action: "none"; Before rollout: "Decide which roles should see site metrics and how long to retain downloaded reports." The standard defines none as nothing to configure or decide, and review as checking fit for an optional capability or new control.
claims.fix: Set action to review: this is a new reporting capability whose default is unknown, with no sourced claim that existing behaviour changes, and the checklist asks administrators to make decisions about its use.

claims.claim: The integration introduces no new end-user behaviour and site visitors are unaffected.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "monitor hub" "read-only" actions; "Power Pages" "monitor hub" "reports" "identifiers". Read the roadmap and monitoring-overview; neither states that collection for this integration has no effects on visitors or end-user behaviour.
claims.fix: Remove the categorical visitor and end-user assurances. State instead that the roadmap describes an admin-center reporting capability for site owners, makers and administrators, and rate impact on that documented audience.
